proof_summary: Finite witness tables establish the required Goldbach and Lemoine decompositions below the two thresholds, while above them parity specializes the assumed representation directly to \(n=p+q\) or \(n=p+2q\). For any bound, choosing a sufficiently large even \(n\) yields the cousin-prime pairs \((q,q+6)\) and \((p-6,p)\); since \(p+q=n\), at least one lower member exceeds the bound, proving infinitude.
